source_record.authority: The General Chapter of 1677, under Innocent Le Masson, Prior of the Grande Chartreuse and General of the Order
source_record.citation:
Printed on the engraved title page of the 1679 edition, READ HERE IN THE PAGE
IMAGE on 2026-08-02 and no longer taken from the catalogue: `MISSALE CARTVSIANI
/ Ordinis ex ordinatione Capituli Generalis. / Anno Domini M.D.C.LXXVII. /
Celebrati Sub R.P.D. Innocentio le Masson Priore / Cartusiæ ac totius eiusdem
ordinis Generali` [verified, canvas f5 of ark:/12148/bpt6k9127828m].

THE CATALOGUE'S TYPO IS THE CATALOGUE'S. Gallica's record transcribes the last
words as `totius eiusdem odinis generali`; the engraved plate reads `ordinis`
plainly. The earlier state of this row reproduced `odinis` and flagged it as the
catalogue's own -- that flag was right, and it is now settled at the plate
instead of being a guess about a transcription.

THE ORDINANCE ITSELF IS PRINTED IN THE BOOK, which is better evidence than the
title page and was not previously known to this file. Innocent Le Masson's
prefatory letter at canvas f7, headed `FRATER INNOCENTIVS, Humilis Prior Majoris
Cartusiæ, ac totius Ordinis Cartusiensis Minister Generalis`, recites it and
then quotes its tenor [verified in the page image]: `... ordinationem in Capitulo
Generali anni 1677. edidimus, cujus tenorem hic referre placet. [Quia Missalium
penuria laboramus, ordinamus Missalia ad vsum Ordinis de novo imprimi, ac
propterea monemus Visitatores Provinciarum & Priores Domorum, vt si quid in
ipsis ... addendum` -- the sentence runs onto the following leaf, which was not
fetched, and is therefore cut here at the catchword rather than completed from
guesswork.
source_record.date_note:
TWO YEARS ARE IN PLAY AND THEY ARE NOT COLLAPSED. The chapter met in 1677; the
book was printed in 1679. The station is dated by the PRINTING, 1679, because
that is the state the line reached, and the chapter's year is in `authority` and
in the citation rather than being averaged into the date.

BOTH YEARS ARE NOW VERIFIED ON ONE LEAF, which is the cleanest possible warrant
for keeping them apart: the engraved title plate at canvas f5 carries `Anno
Domini M.D.C.LXXVII.` in its title and `1679` in its imprint at the foot of the
same plate [verified 2026-08-02]. Le Masson's letter at f7 names the chapter
year a third time, as `Capitulo Generali anni 1677`.
source_record.effect: No departure. No unit of this use has been read.

TWO FACTS ABOUT THE COPY, recorded because neither was in this file. The
digitised exemplar is NOT a BnF copy: the manifest labels it `Bibliothèque
municipale de Grenoble, Vh.258 Rés.`, Gallica hosts it as part of the Grenoble

does not carry, is engraved at the foot of that plate: `FAVRATII IN SABAVDIA /

Cartusiæ / 1679`, signed `L. Cossin Sculpsit` -- printed at Fourvoirie in Savoy
at the charge of the Grande Chartreuse.

source_record.citation: Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship, Celebrationis eucharisticae, Prot. n. 166/70, 26 March 1970, printed at the head of the 1970 typical edition; registered as work.holy-see.decretum-de-editione-typica-missalis-romani-1970.
source_record.dateline: Ex adibus Sacre Congregationis pro Cultu Divino, die 26 martii anni 1970, Feria V in Cena Domini.
source_record.effect: Carries every departure this file records for the Ordinary of the Mass.
source_record.effect_note:
TWO WITNESSES OF ONE DECREE WERE COMPARED HERE, and the comparison is the
opposite of the one the base slice made. Both the 1970 typical edition's text
layer and the 2002 typical edition's print this decree, and both were read here:
the 1970 scan renders `eucharistice`, `Pontice`, `Pontihicis`, `adibus` and
`Sacre`, while the 2002 file renders `eucharisticae`, `Pontifice`, `Pontificis`,
`aedibus` and `Sacrae`. The wording is the same; one delivery loses the ae
ligature and one does not. A diff of the two would report eight changes to a

source_record.effect_note:
THIS STATION IS THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE THAT KEEPS A GENERALISATION HONEST, and it
is why the exempt-uses line is drawn the way it is. The two signatories here --
Cardinal Vico as Prefect and Alexander Verde as Secretary -- are THE SAME TWO MEN
who signed the Roman typical edition's decree of 25 July 1920, in the same
offices, four years apart. So the diocesan uses do not legislate their own
typical editions: Rome does, through the same congregation.

And yet no edge is drawn from the Roman line into this one. One congregation
acting for two rites is a fact about who signs, not a descent of one rite from
the other, and drawing it would make the Braga use look like a branch of the
Roman typical editions. The distinction between an authority and a lineage is
exactly what this file's edges exist to keep.

CORRECTED 2026-08-01. This station carried `act_citation = "not-found"` from the
day it was drawn until the missal acquisition audit read the decree. The
correction, and why the error was made, are both worth keeping.

THE DECREE EXISTS AND HAS NOW BEEN READ, at page 2 of the Vatican typical
edition, in the exact facsimile this repository already had registered. Opening,
with the OCR damage of that text layer reproduced (`rubricanim`, `i960`):

  DECRETUM
  Novo rubricanim corpore, a Summo Pontifice Ioanne XXIII, Motu proprio
  << Rubricarum instructum >> diei 23 iulii anno i960 approbato posteroque die
  a Sacra Rituum Congregatione promulgato, vix fieri non potuit quin eadem
  Sacra Rituum Congregatio novam Missalis romani editionem, ad dictum
  rubricarum codicem plane accommodatam, pararet.

Operative clause: `hinc est quod praesens Vaticana Missalis romani editio uti
<< typica >> declaratur`. Dateline: `Romae, ex aedibus Sacrae Rituum
Congregationis, die 23 iunii 1962`, subscribed `A. M. Card. LARRAONA, S. R. C.
Praefectus` and `Henricus Dante, S. R. C. a secretis`.

So the incipit `Novo rubricarum corpore`, which this file expressly declined to
promote because it was known only from a report, is now read from the book.

WHY THE ERROR WAS MADE, because it is instructive and not careless. This
tracer's corpus is seven Internet Archive OCR text layers, and its 1962 witness
is the BENZIGER printing, which carries a New York imprimatur and not the
Vatican decree. The statement `only three occurrences of DECRETUM in 136,068
lines` was true of that scan. What was false was recording the result in a field
that reads as a claim about the repository -- because the repository held the
decree, in a passage record dated 2026-07-25, six days before this file was
written:
`passage.catholic-church.missale-romanum.vatican-typica-1962.decretum-sacrae-rituum-congregationis-1962`,
states `verified`, locus `front matter, artifact PDF p. 2`.

Two records of one fact, in one tree, never compared. guidance/the-shape.md
section 2. `act_citation` is `cited-externally` rather than `cited-in-corpus`
because the decree stands in the Vatican typical edition, which is not a witness
of this file's corpus; the corpus is unchanged and its own negative result
stands as reported.

attested in `benziger-iuxta-typicam-1962` -- a New York printing declared to

source_record.root_basis:
The record of this line starts here. The Braga use is far older -- a 1558
printing is at the Bibliotheque nationale de France and a 1498 printing is
recorded with no digital facsimile located -- and neither is carried in this run,
so no edge is drawn into this station.

That makes this line unusual and worth noticing: it is the ONLY use line in this
file whose root is an act rather than a printing.

THE 1558 PRINTING WAS REACHED AND READ ON 2026-08-02, and this root is kept
anyway. It is BnF Réserve B-1478, 554 canvases, `Missale juxta usum & ordinem
Almae Bracarensis Ecclesiae Hispaniarum Primatis`, dated 1558 by Gallica's own
record, and its shelfmark is pencilled on the flyleaf at canvas f4 beside the
reference `Weale 198` [verified]. Two things in it are worth a later lane's
attention and NEITHER IS ASSERTED AS AN ACT HERE:

  1.  IT CARRIES WHAT LOOKS LIKE ITS OWN PROMULGATING INSTRUMENT. Canvas f5 is a
      letter headed `BALTHASAR LIMPVS ARCHIEPISCOPVS ET BRACARAE Dominus,
      Hispaniarum Primas: Decano & Capitulo sanctae Bracarensis Ecclesiae, ac
      totius eius prouinciae Clero sanctum exoptat spiritum & salutem in Domino
      sempiternam`, in which Archbishop Baltasar Limpo describes finding the old
      missal `corruptum illud certe vetustate` and having a corrected edition
      made [verified in the page image]. That is an archbishop of Braga ordering
      a Braga missal, four hundred years before the act this line is rooted on.
      IT IS NOT ADDED AS A STATION IN THIS RUN: the letter was read but not
      transcribed whole, it carries no date in the portion read, and adding a
      root below an existing root is a change to the line's shape rather than an
      evidence upgrade. It is the single most promising lead for extending this
      line backwards and it is written down so it is not re-found.

  2.  IT WAS PRINTED AT LYON, NOT AT BRAGA. Gallica's record gives the imprint
      as `Lugduni sumptibus Jo. à Burgundia, bibliopolae regis Lusitanorum,
      1558` [verified] -- at Lyon, at the charge of Jean de Bourgogne, bookseller
      to the King of Portugal. Worth recording because this file carries a
      Lyonnais line as well, and a reader meeting `Lugduni` on a Braga book
      should not take it for a use.

  3.  ONE CAUTION ON THE COPY. Its first printed leaf in the digitisation is the
      Limpo letter; no printed title page was found in the leaves examined, and
      the BnF describes the preliminaries as `[10]` leaves. Whether the title
      leaf is absent from this copy was NOT established, and it is flagged
      rather than resolved.

QUO PRIMUM IS NO LONGER A ROOT. The base slice drew it as one and said in terms
that it took no position on what preceded it. This slice goes earlier, and the
edge it draws is not a guess: the bull's own opening recites the Tridentine
decree that committed the missal to the Pope. An act that says what it is
executing has drawn its own edge.

The base slice's root basis is kept, not deleted, and is printed as superseded.
It was correct about its own corpus, and a record that quietly stops saying
something it once said is a record a reader cannot check.

source_record.root_basis_superseded:
Superseded on 2026-08-01 by the edge above. What it said:

  The earliest act this tracer represents. It is not the beginning of the Roman
  Mass and is not offered as one: what stands before it -- the pre-Tridentine
  curial missal, the 1474 Milan printing, the diocesan uses out of which the
  Tridentine commission worked -- is a live question this tracer takes no
  position on and draws no edge into. A root here means "this record starts

uses: this slice draws NO edge from any of them into Quo primum either, and the
pre-Tridentine Roman printings it does carry stand on their own line and stop

The earliest act this file carries, and it is not offered as the beginning of
anything. What stands before it -- the mediaeval Roman curial missal, the
sacramentaries behind that, the uses out of which all of them grew -- is not
represented here and no edge is drawn into this station. A root means the record
starts here.

It is the earliest act rather than the Session XXV decree because it is the
